newsitem.title: USA: Northeast to pay nuke workers back overtime.
newsitem.headline: Northeast to pay nuke workers back overtime.

text.p: Northeast Utilities will pay workers at three nuclear facilities back overtime after the company reclassified 27 job titles for 123 employees from exempt to non-exempt status.
Exempt positions are usually not entitled to financial compensation for overtime work.
The Hartford, Conn., utility will reimburse $320,000 in overtime compensation (pre-tax) for a two-year period between Aug 1, 1994 and Sept 14, 1996, said NU spokeswoman Deborah Beauchamp.

The change in job classifications at the Seabrook, N.H., nuclear facility was prompted by a request from an onsite worker, and at the Millstone and Connecticut Yankee nuclear power plants by a recently completed U.S. Department of Labor audit, she said.
Beauchamp said the affected jobs were "line roles" such as senior engineer designers and electrical test coordinators.
The reclassification will take effect Sunday, she added.
Current and former NU nuclear employees--52 at Seabrook; 62 at Millstone and nine at Connecticut Yankee who were entitled to the back pay--could receive the compensation today, she said.
The company continues to evaluate its organization and compensation for its employees, she said. "Additional reclassification is possible."
